## Description

A peritrich with cup-shaped zooids (90–120 × 25–50 µm) on a **non-contractile**, branched stalk that
forms colonies up to 4 mm. Unlike *Vorticella*, the stalk has no spasmoneme: the zooid contracts, not
the stalk. It filters bacteria with the peristomal crown.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: `pond` (weight 0.15), `puddle` (weight 0.15); 3 individuals in a reference drop at weight 1.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

A [rigid stalk](../../mechanics/stalks-and-colonies.md) with longitudinal striations; colonial, daughters stay on
dichotomous branches (up to 12 zooids here). The zooid is a [bell](../../mechanics/shape-changes.md) that closes on
a sudden current (mechanoreception, threshold estimated). It divides longitudinally; one daughter
leaves as a telotroch.

## Not implemented yet

- Colonies are much smaller than the real 4 mm.
- Stalks do not collide with cells ([bug](../../bugs/stalks-and-tails-do-not-collide.md)).

## Unique and shared mechanics

Shares the bell zooid, longitudinal division and telotroch with all peritrichs; the rigid stalk with
suctorians.
